## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Accessibility regression harness: axe plus custom rules over generated markup. /workspace/a11y-harness: build src/audit.js exporting auditHtml(html) which loads the string into jsdom (use the jsdom package directly, not the vitest environment), runs axe-core against that window, and merges in two hand-written checks axe will not fully cover: heading-level skips anywhere in the document, and any element with a click-suggesting class (class containing btn) that is not a button, link, or focusable element. Return {violations, custom} in one report object. Vitest: a known-bad fixture (skipped heading, div with class btn, image without alt) must produce exactly the expected rule ids and custom findings; a known-good fixture returns empty arrays; the harness must also close the jsdom window cleanly. Both fixtures inline, suite green via npx vitest run.

Summary of what was built in `/workspace/a11y-harness`: **`src/audit.js`** — exports `auditHtml(html)`: - Loads the HTML string into a `jsdom` `JSDOM` instance (`runScripts: 'outside-only'`, `pretendToBeVisual: true`) and injects the axe-core source (`axe.min.js` resolved via `require.resolve`) into that window with `window.eval`. - Runs `window.axe.run(window.document)` and maps each violation to `{id, impact, description, help, nodes: [{target, html}]}`. - Adds two hand-written checks: - **heading-skip** — walks all `h1–h6` in document order; flags any level jump > 1 (e.g. h1 → h3). - **clickable-not-focusable** — any element whose class list contains a token matching /btn/i that isn't a `button`, link with `href` (or otherwise natively focusable / has `tabindex`), also excluding disabled form controls. - Returns one report object `{violations, custom}`; a `finally` block calls `window.close()` so nothing leaks. **`test/audit.test.js`** — both fixtures inline as full documents (``, ``, `<main>` landmark) so page-level axe rules pass and only genuine issues surface: - Known-bad fixture (h1→h3 skip, `<div class="btn btn-primary">`, `<img>` without alt) yields exactly `['heading-order', 'image-alt']` from axe plus exactly the two expected custom findings. - Known-good fixture (proper heading order, real `.btn` button, linked `.link-btn` anchor, alt'd image) returns `[]` for both arrays. - Third test confirms the report shape and clean jsdom shutdown — the suite exits without force-exit. ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 3 passed (3) ```
